genius.notes: Reviewed 2026-10-07. Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A. is the sole current USDtb issuer and obligor under its covered-stablecoin terms. The OCC's active national trust-bank list confirms charter 25243; this existing charter does not establish token-specific GENIUS PPSI approval. Anchorage's May 1, 2026 comment letter states that it expects to become a PPSI once the Act is effective, supporting issuer-announced-intent and the announced federal-qualified-nonbank pathway, rather than an official application or approval. Client redemption is at USD 1 par value, net applicable fees, subject to onboarding and other contractual conditions; non-client holders have no enforceable direct contractual redemption right until accepted as clients. The public August 31, 2026 reserve examination, signed September 28, compares USD 530,419,653 of reserve assets with 529,269,213 redeemable USDtb tokens and reports BUIDL plus cash. The examination explicitly excludes a legal or regulatory compliance opinion. Treasury describes January 18, 2027 as the expected Act effective date and July 18, 2028 as the general DASP offer-sale restriction date. Its September 30 SCRC procedural rule does not approve an issuer. No current token-specific GENIUS action was located in this review; Anchorage's 2022 bank-level consent order was terminated August 18, 2025 and its 2021 operating agreement was terminated February 9, 2026. The enforcement field concerns located current token-specific action, not absence of historical bank supervision.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, no public token-specific GENIUS PPSI approval or official pending PPSI application was located for Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A. or USDtb in the sources and name searches checked. Its existing bank charter and reserve reports establish regulated-bank issuance and public reporting, not GENIUS authorization. Its own May 1 filing expressly describes expected future PPSI status. No current token-specific GENIUS enforcement action was located; the separately identified historical bank-level orders were terminated. The finding is limited to reviewed public evidence and does not exclude nonpublic or newly posted filings.
